messages:
samir_sRE: FYI customer 'Brightwell' (private deployment rw-priv-usw) reporting intermittent 502/timeout to private API since ~03:00 UTC after they pushed a firewall policy change. Internal DNS for service endpoints also failing. Can we triage?

liz_eng: Assigned. Any repro steps or packet traces from the customer?

samir_sRE: Repro steps from Brightwell: 1) curl https://internal-api.service.svc.cluster.local/health -> times out 2) dig @10.10.0.2 internal-api.service.svc.cluster.local -> SERVFAIL 3) traceroute to 10.10.0.2 stops at peer (10.254.1.1)

marie_net: Can you paste their peering attachment ID and whether this is DX or IPsec?

samir_sRE: It's DirectConnect private virtual interface via partner — attachment pvif-0b7c3a and bgp session with customer ASN 65551. They said they rotated firewall rules right before it started.

liz_eng: Ok. First things: check BGP status and IKE/IPsec (if they have VPN fallback) and confirm UDP 500/4500 to our egress is allowed. Also check route filter on our side.

marie_net: Running quick checks from our side: show bgp summary -> their peer shows Established then drops a few times. I see frequent BGP keepalive flaps around 03:02-03:05 UTC. Also noticed our route filter for pvif-0b7c3a had no explicit allow for their internal prefixes after the recent change.

samir_sRE: Customer sent tcpdump snippet (they NAT through edge fw):
```
12:04:56.123456 IP 203.0.113.45.4500 > 198.51.100.12.4500: UDP, length 128
12:04:56.126000 IP 198.51.100.12.4500 > 203.0.113.45.4500: UDP, length 128
12:04:56.220000 IP 203.0.113.45.179 > 198.51.100.12.179: Flags [S], seq 0
12:04:56.223000 IP 198.51.100.12.179 > 203.0.113.45.179: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
12:05:02.000000 IP 203.0.113.45 > 198.51.100.12: ICMP port-unreachable
```
\nsamir_sRE: They also show occasional ICMP port-unreachable around the BGP/TCP packets.

liz_eng: ICMP port-unreachable from firewall typically means stateful block for the related ephemeral UDP. Could be NAT-T translations timing out or firewall treating UDP 4500 as ephemeral and dropping. But BGP TCP 179 is establishing then RST/ICMP; suspicious.

marie_net: I pulled our flow logs for pvif-0b7c3a. I see accepted inbound TCP 179, but egress from our side to 203.0.113.0/24 shows DENY for UDP 4500/500 on a security policy that was tightened on 2025-11-06 02:58 UTC (matches their rotation).

samir_sRE: Customer confirmed they tightened egress to only allow specific ports and forgot to include NAT traversal ports. They allowed TCP 443/80 but not UDP 4500/500.

tony_oncall: Quick checklist: allow UDP 500 and 4500, allow TCP 179 (BGP), ensure route-filter contains customer prefixes, check MD5 on BGP if configured, verify MTU/clamps.

samir_sRE: I asked Brightwell to temporarily allow UDP 500/4500 and TCP 179 to test. Waiting on their change now.

deploy-bot: Notified: runbook 'private-peering-bgp-ipsec-checklist' suggested.

(10 minutes pass)

samir_sRE: Brightwell updated firewall to allow UDP/500 and UDP/4500 and left TCP/179 allowed. Re-tested: curl now returns 200, dig resolves correctly. Traceroute reaches 10.10.0.2.

marie_net: Confirmed BGP stable, no more flaps. Our route-filter was missing one internal prefix (10.10.128.0/18) — I re-added it to avoid asymmetric routing.

liz_eng: Any TLS errors originally? Customer mentioned TLS handshake failures in logs earlier.

samir_sRE: They reported TLS timeouts but those were side-effect of connection timeouts. Once connectivity restored, TLS handshakes succeed. They had also rotated a proxy policy that briefly stripped SNI for internal hostnames — fixed on their side.

tony_oncall: Root cause summary: customer firewall tightened egress rules removing NAT-T (UDP 4500/500) -> IPsec NAT traversal intermittently failed + BGP flaps due to partial drops -> DNS / API timeouts. Contributing factor: our route-filter missed one internal prefix after the partner provisioning change.

samir_sRE: Customer confirms degraded for ~20m, now healthy. Filing KB: add automated monitor to detect missing UDP 4500/500 flows and BGP hold-time flaps for pvif attachments. Also recommend adding a preflight validator we run on peering changes to catch route-filter gaps.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2025-1187 updated to Resolved. Follow-up assigned to 'net-eng' for route-filter hardening.

liz_eng: Nice triage. Can someone add the firewall checklist to the private-deploy runbook? :thumbsup:

marie_net: I'll add the checklist and create an alert rule for BGP flap rate > 3/min.

samir_sRE: closing from support side. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
